title: GE warns 2018 could be worse than expected for its power business
主要内容: General Electric (GE) has warned that 2018 could be a more challenging year for its power business than previously anticipated. GE Chief Executive John Flannery stated that issues from 2017 are expected to carry over into 2018, but the power unit remains a strong franchise. The market for GE's gas turbines has been weak due to the growth of renewable energy sources like wind and solar. GE is preparing for its worst year of gas turbine installations in about 15 years, with expected orders as low as 30 gigawatts. In 2017, final orders were anticipated to be less than 35 gigawatts. Profit in the power segment dropped 88% in the final quarter of 2017, driven by market conditions, execution issues, and other charges. GE still produces about a third of the world's electricity and holds 50% market share in advanced power technology. The company plans to focus on adjusting its manufacturing footprint, improving cash and project execution, maximizing value from its installed base, and enhancing management processes. GE Power announced 12,000 layoffs in December and has scaled back 15 manufacturing sites. Russell Stokes, president of GE Power, noted that the unit has increased its ability to monitor outages, raising visibility from less than 30% to nearly 80% of its installed base. Servicing equipment more efficiently represents a $2 billion opportunity. GE also faces challenges in the renewable energy space, with pressure to lower prices on wind turbines. The company expects profits to be down significantly in the first quarter of 2018 due to fewer wind turbine shipments in the U.S. and ongoing price pressure. GE shares fell 1% after the company disclosed an SEC review of its accounting practices.
